bc_grand_forks.blurb: The climbing around the city of Grand Forks, in British Columbia's Boundary Country, is mostly sport with a smaller share of trad, and most routes are 5.8 to 5.10, with plenty of short, friendly sport lines. It centres on four areas: Gilpin Grasslands, which holds the most climbs, Cascade Gorge, North Fork and Observation Mountain. The Gilpin crags are best from March to June and too hot in July and August, while Cascade Gorge is the coolest place to climb in summer. At Granby Dam and the Cascade Gorge bridge some of the climbing is on stacked granite blocks, thin and technical in feel. Newer routes tend to have short approaches.

ca_high_desert_bouldering.blurb: High Desert Bouldering gathers scattered boulder areas of California's high desert, in the Barstow direction. Nearly everything is bouldering, and most problems are on the easy side, V2 or below, with only a few reaching V6 or V7. Wagon Wheel, east of Ridgecrest in the Mojave Desert, holds the most climbs: its grey granite boulders lie in every direction, with plenty of room to explore. House of the Setting Sun, also called the Ammo Dump, sits on the south side of a ridge and has big, steep boulders with good holds and flat ground beneath them. Edwards AFB has a handful of problems.

ca_split_rocks_west.blurb: Split Rocks West covers the formations lying west of the paved road in the Split Rocks section of Pinto Basin, Joshua Tree National Park. It holds trad, sport and a few top-rope routes. Most climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.11, centred on 5.10, with a scattering of easier and harder ones. Isles in the Sky holds the most climbs, then Screamer Rocks and Grand Canyon, with the Rubicon Formation and Graceland smaller. Screamer Rocks has a pair of narrow corridors that give shade and shelter from the wind.

co_beige_tube_area_the_narrows.blurb: Beige Tube Area and The Narrows run along US 34 in Big Thompson Canyon, part of Colorado's Estes Park Valley, reached by following the highway up from Loveland. Sport routes outnumber trad here, with a little bouldering and top-roping. The rock is described as solid gneiss with very little friction, so footwork matters, though loose blocks and scree are a hazard on some walls. The canyon is narrow, with sunlight strongest around midday. Grades are mostly 5.8 to 5.10, with a small group of 5.12 to 5.14 climbs. The Ledges holds the most climbs, followed by Ironing Board Slabs and Anti-Future Crag.

co_deckers.blurb: Deckers, in the South Platte area of Colorado, is a group of rounded granite domes and slabs. Most climbs are one or two pitches of slab, mainly sport with trad and top-rope mixed in, and grades run fairly evenly from 5.6 through 5.11. Bolting is sparse on Atlantis Slab, while Murphy's Dome South Face is mostly friction. Atlantis Slab, Murphy's Dome South Face and the Bali Domes face south, and the south faces can run hot in summer, with fall a good time at Atlantis Slab. Jazz Dome faces south and east. Atlantis Slab holds the most climbs, with Java Dome and Jazz Dome next, and approaches are mostly 10 to 20 minutes.
